memory: I miss spending time with my family and Archie. They bring so much joy to my life. I hope I can make more time for them soon.I remember when we first got Archie. He was so small and fluffy, and he melted my heart the moment I saw him. I spent every moment I could with him during my winter break, teaching him commands and taking him for short walks. It's amazing how big he's gotten now. He's definitely not that little furball anymore!I love how Archie always recognizes my voice on video calls. He goes nuts when he sees me, wagging his tail and whining like he's about to jump through the screen. It's hilarious and heartwarming at the same time. Those moments help me de-stress from coding assignments and debugging sessions. Archie may not perceive images on screens like humans do, but he definitely knows something's up when he hears my voice. It's nice to believe he's looking right at me.I feel really lucky to have such a supportive family. My dad, who's a software engineer, encouraged me to pursue computer science. We used to do coding exercises together in high school, and it sparked my interest in technology. My mom, on the other hand, is a nurse and has a heart of gold. She's always there for me, no matter what. My sister is a ball of energy, always on top of the latest trends and technology. She's going to be a force to be reckoned with in the tech scene. I feel grateful to have such a loving and supportive family.I love our Saturday morning hikes with Archie. He's so full of energy and always excited to explore the trail. Chasing squirrels and sniffing trees is his favorite part. It's a great reminder to appreciate nature and take a break from the hustle and bustle of college life. I'm grateful for these moments with my family and Archie.I cherish the time spent with my extended family, especially my grandparents. They have a special place in my heart, and I'm grateful for the love and support they provide. I still remember the time I accidentally broke my grandma's antique vase, and I'm sure she'll continue to remind me of that for years to come. However, it's the laughter and love we share during holiday gatherings that truly matter. Archie, being the mischievous pup he is, always keeps us entertained, but we have to be careful about what human food he gets his paws on. One year, he got into some leftover turkey bones, and we had to make a late-night vet visit. Since then, we've been extra cautious. Despite the mishaps, I'm thankful for the joy and warmth that comes with spending time with my family.I believe family plays a significant role in shaping who we become. Even as an independent college student, I find that the patience and resilience I've developed through programming projects are influenced by my parents. My dad taught me to stay calm and break down problems, while my mom showed me the importance of being patient and empathetic, even in frustrating situations. My sister also pushes me to stay up-to-date with the latest trends, ensuring I don't fall behind. I often include personal anecdotes, such as stories about Archie or funny moments with my sister, in my scholarship and grad school applications because they hold great significance to me.My family is supportive, close-knit, and lively. They show me what unconditional love looks like, especially when they're fussing over Archie or laughing at his antics. Even with my busy schedule as a fourth-year student, I know I'm always welcome at home, dog hair and all. It's what keeps me going, especially when coding projects don't go as planned. I can always count on my family to recharge me. And when I walk through the door, Archie leaps into my arms, making everything better.
